lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC meeting on August 5, where commissioners will hold public hearings and move toward formal votes on three Land Use Code amendments — including a wildfire areas update and a change to the 'Qualified Owner' definition that touches deed-restricted housing rules. Telluride Town Council follows on August 11 with third reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would rewrite land use and landscaping standards for property owners valleywide. In between, the Telluride Jazz Festival opens Friday and the KOTO Duck Race runs alongside it.

notable.stake: Three Land Use Code amendments go to public hearing and formal vote.
Vote on whether a deed-restricted homeowner can exceed capital improvement limits for a new roof.
Third reading of Wildfire Resiliency Code would amend land use and landscaping rules for all property owners.
Conditional-use permit and architecture reviews for three multifamily projects in Mountain Village.
Ouray County LUC definitions rewrite — changes here quietly shift what the rules allow in practice.
